state:
Query: The vector tile builder drops small islands at zoom 6 to 9 after the simplification change last week; find the context that explains the simplification rule and its tolerance so the fix keeps the intended behaviour for coastlines and lakes
Candidates:
[note:wiki/sessions/a3d7e019.md] Session: coastline import: Imported the new coastline dataset (2026 release). It has more vertices along rocky shores, which made the z4-z8 tiles about 30% larger. I left simplification untouched in this session and opened a follow-up to revisit tolerances. Lakes were not part of this import; they come from the hydrography layer and were unchanged. Timing: the import took 41 minutes on the build host, most of it spent validating ring orientation. Two invalid polygons near the northern fjords were repaired with a zero-width buffer. The follow-up issue lists three options for tolerances (per layer, per zoom, per feature class) but none was chosen in this session, and no code outside the importer changed.
[note:wiki/decisions/vector-simplify.md] Vector simplification: Decision: lines and polygons are simplified with Douglas-Peucker at a tolerance of half a pixel at the target zoom. Polygons whose area falls below 4 square pixels after simplification are dropped, except features tagged keep=always. Coastlines and lakes are simplified the same way; small islands are expected to disappear below z10 unless tagged. Rationale recorded at the time: the 4 square pixel floor removes speckle that made low-zoom tiles noisy and large, and the keep=always tag gives cartographers an escape hatch for islands that matter at low zoom (ferry ports, inhabited islets). The tolerance and the area floor are configured in builder/simplify.toml and are shared by every polygon layer. Changing either affects tile sizes for all layers, so a fix for a single layer should use tags or a per-layer override rather than editing the shared values.
[note:wiki/decisions/tile-size-budget.md] Tile size budget: Decision: a vector tile must stay under 500 KB compressed. When a tile goes over budget the builder first raises the simplification tolerance for that tile, then drops the lowest-priority layers (POIs, then minor roads). It never drops water or land polygons to meet the budget; if still over, it logs a warning and ships the tile. The budget check runs after simplification, so it cannot be the reason a polygon disappears unless the tile was already over budget; the builder log records every tolerance raise with the tile coordinates, which makes it easy to rule this in or out for a given tile.
[note:wiki/notes/island-labels.md] Island labels: Labels for islands use the name tag and are placed at the polygon's pole of inaccessibility. At z6-9 only islands with population tags get labels. This is about labels only; the polygons themselves are handled by the simplification step and are not affected by label rules. Label collisions are resolved by population first, then by area. Unlabelled islands still render as polygons when they survive simplification.
[note:wiki/sessions/f61b2c94.md] Session: z6 render regression: Investigated a hillshade seam at z6 caused by tile edge padding. Fixed by padding rasters with 2 pixels. No vector changes; islands render the same before and after this fix. Screenshots of z6 before and after are attached to the session note; the coastline in both is identical, which also shows the island loss predates this fix.
[note:wiki/decisions/projection-pipeline.md] Projection pipeline: Reproject every source to EPSG:3857 before rasterizing. Vector simplification runs in WGS84 before reprojection, which is why tolerances are expressed in pixels at the target zoom rather than in meters.
rationale: The vector-simplify decision states the tolerance and the rule that drops polygons under 4 square pixels, which is exactly what explains small islands disappearing; the others only touch related topics.
